name: Topiramate
sections: White crystalline powder with bitter taste; a sulfamate-substituted fructose diacetonide; solubility in water ~9.8 mg/mL.

Originally synthesised while researching oral hypoglycaemic agents; approved as an anticonvulsant in 1996 and later for migraine prophylaxis (2004). Generics available from 2006. First approval/introduction: 1996 (discovered 1979 by Maryanoff and Gardocki at McNeil Pharmaceutical / Johnson & Johnson).

Blocks voltage-dependent sodium channels, enhances GABA-A activity, antagonises AMPA/kainate glutamate receptors and weakly inhibits carbonic anhydrase. Receptor / target profile: Multiple targets: voltage-gated sodium and L-type calcium channels, GABA-A potentiation, AMPA/kainate antagonism and carbonic anhydrase (II, IV) inhibition.
Summary: Bioavailability ~80%; Tmax ~2 h. 15–41% protein bound. Mostly excreted unchanged in urine. Half-life ~21 h.
Epilepsy – focal or generalised tonic-clonic seizures (monotherapy and adjunct); Lennox–Gastaut syndrome
Migraine: 25 mg at night for 1 week, increase by 25 mg weekly to 50 mg twice daily (100 mg/day)
Epilepsy monotherapy: 25 mg at night for 1 week, increase by 25–50 mg weekly; usual 100–200 mg/day in two doses (max 500 mg/day)
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
